annotations.text:
AS IT STANDS

Six zeroes greet you before one customer does. The first person waiting is fifth in reading order.

Oxide appears five times on one screen - the law says once. Two of them (the unread tile's left rail, the badge) mean nothing you can act on.

The panel is an imitation of WhatsApp: avatars in random hues, a search pill, bubbles, a round send button. The owner already owns WhatsApp. What this screen can do that the phone cannot is price the ask from the books - and that is the one thing it does not show.

AND THE FAULTS A TEST WOULD CATCH

21px at weight 800 - 800 is not a loaded face, so the browser fakes it. 10.5 / 11.5 / 12.5 / 13.5px are off the ramp. Radii of 11, 12 and 14px where the system has 4 / 6 / 8. A box-shadow on the inbox, where depth is meant to be hairlines.

Names clip without an ellipsis: "Mulongo Hardware & ...", snippet cut to "Ok. And 4...". The customer chip repeats the name already on the row.

And the loudest control on the screen - "Add to Sourcing" - is acting on a wrong guess: the shop sells cement.

DIRECTION A - THE ASKS COME FIRST

One screen. The queue is people waiting, not chats; a row opens in place - the same component the cash book and consignment already use - and inside it sits the transcript, what the ask matched to in the catalogue at today's price, and the reply already written.

Posting and broadcasts stop being rooms and become a rail. The tab strip goes, so the app is two levels deep again instead of three.

One oxide button on the page: Send the price.

TRADE-OFF: reaching a chat nobody is waiting on now costs a search. That is the bet - this screen is for the day's unanswered money, not for browsing history.

DIRECTION B - THE THREE ROOMS KEPT

Same information, less rebuilding. Inbox / Today's post / Broadcasts survive as a segmented control in the page header rather than a third row of navigation, and the chat list is a dense list of rows - no avatars, no hues, no fake search pill - beside the same priced thread.

TRADE-OFF: you still have to notice which of 41 chats is waiting. The list sorts by time, not by who is owed an answer, so the screen hands you a filing cabinet where A hands you a queue.

Cheaper to build, and it fixes the vocabulary. It does not fix the reading order.

THE FOUR STATES

Not connected is where every new shop starts, and today it is a developer's manual - npx, system-user tokens, webhook URLs - printed at a shop owner. Here it says what is missing, what it costs in time, and offers to mail the technical steps to whoever set up the computer.

The closed reply window is stated before you type, not after the send fails. A refused message names itself and says the books are untouched.

And an empty queue names the one thing still outstanding rather than sitting blank.

BUILT.

Direction A is in index.html now, on branch claude/whatsapp-page-design-fvh71u. This artboard was updated to match what actually shipped, so the canvas is not a picture of something that does not exist.

Two things the code decides that a still frame cannot show: the matched reply is written straight INTO the composer, and it may replace only what this screen last wrote — a reply the owner typed is never overwritten. And the assistant's draft outranks the token match when both are live.

The phone is a genuinely separate design: the layer hides the desk row at 820px and shows a card, both emitted from one call. Its figure is the WAIT, because on this screen that is what the money is measured in.

WHY IT READS AS ONE THING

The panel has one header and five jobs under it, and every boundary between them is the same 1px hairline. The house's grouping device is the 34px panel header — there is exactly one, at the very top — so below it the eye has nothing to group by.

Two of the five jobs were never about today's post. "What limits the picks" is a fact about the catalogue, and The channel panel already reports it ("62 of 480 in the catalogue") — the same thing was being said twice, in two panels, in different words.

And two real faults, both reproduced at 1440 with a 480-product catalogue:

"16 of 7" — the figure counts POSTS, the label says DAYS.

The gap rows clip. The row was taught to wrap at phone widths; nobody checked the 304px rail, which is narrower than the phone.

The fix wraps the row's TEXT, not its button — pushing the control to a second line makes every row two lines tall and blurs the boundary all over again.

THE ALGORITHM, REWRITTEN AROUND ONE QUESTION

What is this post expected to EARN? Everything becomes shillings, so the terms can finally be compared. Today they cannot: +3 for a restock, +3.6 for asks, +5 for sitting, -0.25 for no photo — eight bonuses on no shared unit, and nobody ever chose those ratios against each other.

Expected profit = margin per unit x expected extra units.

Margin is the sell price less the last price actually paid, from a purchase invoice. Expected extra units is LEARNED: for every recorded post, units sold in the seven days after against the seven before, grouped by the KIND of reason the post carried. The shop has posted 39 times and the algorithm has never once looked at what happened next — that is the biggest thing wrong with it.

Signals it should use and does not: the inbox (waQuoteMatch already turns a message into a product), WhatsApp-born orders, whether the product is in the tappable catalogue, and rival prices, which exist per variant and are the most postable fact a hardware shop owns.

Two channels, two bars. Status is free, so anything positive is worth posting. A broadcast is paid, so it must clear what Meta charges to send it — shown as arithmetic, not as a recommendation.

WHAT IT REFUSES TO SAY

Lift is association, not proof. A busy week lifts everything, and this measures a correlation on a small sample with no control. So the panel says "what tends to go with a post here", never "posting caused this", and it names how many posts each row rests on.

Before about ten posts it shows no estimate at all — it ranks on margin and stated demand, both facts the books already hold, and says plainly that it does not know the rest yet. The third artboard is that state.

The broadcast multiplier is the one number with no evidence behind it: whether a broadcast is seen more often than a status. It starts at 1.0 and the screen carries a warning saying so until there are broadcasts to learn from.

Stuck stock loses its own term under a profit objective — it needs somewhere else to live, and What to buy is probably its home.
